speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have had a tympanoplasty and are now experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings. How long has this pain been occurring since your surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Otitis Media / Cholesteatoma recurrence.
Based on your history of recurrent infections and the new onset of shooting pain specifically when chewing (suggesting Eustachian tube dysfunction or referred pain), along with discomfort from earrings, I suspect a complication like a cholesteatoma or granulation tissue at the graft site. Given your history of depression and chronic infections, we must also consider the impact of stress on your immune response and healing.

Let's confirm this with some imaging. REQUEST IMAGES: CT Temporal_Bone.
